title: Signal-detection replication of labels and literacy guide
rationale: The source study found Automated Flagging raised accuracy 4.4 points (CI 1.4 to 7.3) and the AI Literacy Guide 4.7 points (CI 0.2 to 9.2), but pooled accuracy was only 1 point (CI -0.3 to 2.4) across 44 uncorrected tests. Only share-correct scores were stored, so sensitivity and response bias could not be separated, and Breathing and Nudge arms raised AI detection without raising authentic recognition.
contribution: Estimates d' and criterion separately for the two nominally effective interventions in a powered, preregistered replication with item-level data.
limitations: Two interventions only; others from the source study are not retested.
Item-level flagging within subject may interact with the between-subject arm.
Online US panel; stimuli set differs from the original 24 posts.
Signal-detection model assumes equal-variance Gaussian evidence unless confidence data show otherwise.

design.title: Signal-detection replication of labels and literacy guide
design.overview: Respondents are randomised to control, automated-detector label, or AI literacy guide. They then judge 40 images (20 AI, 20 authentic), giving real/AI judgments and 1-6 confidence for each. In the label arm and the other arms alike, each item is randomly shown with or without a detector flag, except that the flag is only displayed in the label arm.
design.hypothesis: Automated labels and the literacy guide raise d' relative to control; if the effects are only criterion shifts, d' will not differ and c will move toward more AI responses.
design.primaryOutcome: Sensitivity d' and criterion c from a multilevel signal-detection model (probit mixed model of AI judgment on true item status, arm, and their interaction, with random effects for respondent and item).
design.comparison: Each treatment arm versus control on d' and c; Holm correction across the two primary d' contrasts; criterion contrasts secondary; within-arm flagged versus unflagged items exploratory.
design.population: US adults from an online panel, about 420 per arm (1,260 total), with preregistered exclusions for failed attention check, speeding, and duplicate responses.

conditions.title: Automated detector label
conditions.description: Randomly selected items carry a machine-learning detector label.

conditions.title: AI Literacy Guide
conditions.description: A guide with examples of AI artifacts is read before the task.

questions.text: You are invited to a research study about how people judge online images. It takes about 10 minutes and is voluntary. You may stop at any time. Do you agree to participate?
Have you ever interacted with any of the following tools? Please check all that apply. If you have not interacted with any of these tools, skip to the next question.

Please read this guide on spotting AI-generated images. It explains common artifacts such as distorted hands and text, inconsistent lighting and shadows, overly smooth textures, and odd backgrounds, with side-by-side examples of AI and authentic images. Spend at least one minute on it.

You will now see 40 images. For each, say whether it is AI-generated or authentic, then rate your confidence. Some images may carry a label from an automated AI-detection tool. Go with your gut if unsure.

blocks.title: Judgment task (40 items, order randomised; item template repeated for items 1 to 40)

questions.text: Is this image AI-generated or authentic?
How confident are you in that answer? (1 = not at all, 6 = completely)
Please answer the following question about artificial intelligence.

rows.text: I feel confident in my ability to detect artificial intelligence.

questions.text: Thank you. Some images were AI-generated and some authentic, and any detector labels were randomly assigned and may not have been accurate. The study examines how people judge AI media.
Thank you for your time. You will not continue the study.

flow.label: item1
flow.value: [IMAGE: one of 40 photos, half AI-generated and half authentic, with a detector label shown for a random half of items in the label arm only]

assumptions: Target about 420 per arm (1,260 total): 80% power to detect 0.03; H1 observed 0.044 (Automated Flagging) shrunk toward the 0.03 MDE of the largest arm (0.0318 at n=333); a 3-point gain at 80% power needs roughly 420 per arm.
Online US panel; compensation per panel norms.
Exclusions (failed attention check, speeding, duplicates) and Holm correction across the two d' contrasts are preregistered before fielding.
The item block is programmed as 40 loops of the item template, with item order and flag status randomised by the platform.
unresolved: The 40 image files, their ground-truth labels and the detector label assets must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and participant compensation must be supplied.
The treatment block for the control arm is intentionally empty; the label arm's flags are shown inside the item stimuli.
